description: Implement destructuring, splat/spread, variadic procs, and streams — core language features forming a dependency chain that unlocks lazy evaluation and the foundation for shell interop.

userStories.title: Positional vector destructuring
userStories.description: As a JACL programmer, I want to destructure vectors with `def [a b c] $v` so that I can bind multiple values from a vector in one statement.
acceptanceCriteria: Parser recognizes `[a b c]` as a destructuring pattern on the LHS of `def` and `mut` (operator forms `=` and `:` too)
New AST node type AST_DESTRUCTURE_VEC created with child nodes for each binding name
New opcode OP_DESTRUCTURE_VEC with operand N: pops vector from stack, extracts N elements by index, pushes each onto stack
Compiler emits OP_DESTRUCTURE_VEC when it sees AST_DESTRUCTURE_VEC in a def/mut context
VM executes OP_DESTRUCTURE_VEC: runtime error if value is not a vector, runtime error if vector length != N
`def [a b c] [vec 1 2 3]` binds a=1, b=2, c=3 as local variables
`mut [a b] [vec 1 2]` creates mutable bindings a=1, b=2
Works at any scope depth (top-level globals and nested blocks)
Typed destructuring: `def [i64 a, i64 b] $v` checks element types at compile time when types are known

E2e test file test/test_destructure_vec.c: tests using jacl_run() verify correct binding values via print output for basic destructuring, nested scope, typed, mut, length-mismatch error, and non-vector error
All existing tests pass
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra
userStories.notes: Destructuring `def [a b c] $expr` compiles to: compile RHS (pushes one value), emit OP_DESTRUCTURE_VEC 3 which pops the vector and pushes elements 0,1,2 onto stack, then each becomes a local via the normal def path. For globals (scope_depth==0), each extracted value needs OP_DEF_GLOBAL. Parser change: in the def/mut path, check if the next token after `def` is TOKEN_LBRACKET — if so, parse as destructuring pattern instead of a variable name. The operator desugaring (= and :) already converts to def/mut AST nodes, so destructuring works with operators automatically.

userStories.title: Named struct/map destructuring
userStories.description: As a JACL programmer, I want to destructure structs with `def {x, y} $point` so that I can extract named fields into scope.
acceptanceCriteria: Parser recognizes `{x, y}` as a destructuring pattern on the LHS of `def` and `mut`
New AST node type AST_DESTRUCTURE_NAMED created with field name children
New opcode OP_DESTRUCTURE_STRUCT with operand encoding field names: pops struct/map from stack, extracts named fields, pushes each
Compiler emits struct-field extraction (OP_STRUCT_GET_FIELD by offset) when struct type is known at compile time
Compiler emits map-key lookup (OP_MAP_GET by string key) when type is dyn/map
Compile-time error if struct type is known and a field name in the pattern doesn't exist on that struct
Runtime error for maps if a key from the pattern is missing
`def {x, y} $point` binds x and y from Point struct fields
Field order in the pattern doesn't matter: `def {y, x} $point` works identically
`mut {x, y} $point` creates mutable bindings
Typed field destructuring: `def {i32 x, i32 y} $point` type-checks fields at compile time

E2e test file test/test_destructure_named.c: tests using jacl_run() verify correct binding values for struct destructuring, map destructuring, field-order independence, mut, typed, missing-field error (compile-time and runtime)
All existing tests pass
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra
userStories.notes: Parser change: in the def/mut path, check if the next token is TOKEN_LBRACE — if so, parse comma-separated field names (with optional type prefixes) as a destructuring pattern. For struct extraction: use StructTypeRegistry to look up field offsets and emit OP_STRUCT_GET_FIELD for each. For map extraction: emit OP_MAP_GET with the field name as a string key. The compiler needs the RHS type to decide which path — if it can infer the struct type from the expression, use struct path; otherwise fall back to map path.

userStories.title: Wildcard pattern in destructuring
userStories.description: As a JACL programmer, I want to use `_` in destructuring patterns to ignore values I don't need.
acceptanceCriteria: Parser recognizes `_` as a wildcard in positional destructuring patterns: `def [_ b _] $v`
Wildcard positions are marked in the AST node (e.g., null name or special flag)
Compiler skips binding creation for wildcard positions — no local variable allocated, no extraction bytecode emitted for those positions
OP_DESTRUCTURE_VEC updated to support skip mask: skipped positions don't push values onto stack
`_` does not create a binding — referencing `$_` after destructuring is an undefined variable error
Multiple `_` in the same pattern is allowed (they don't conflict with each other)
`def {x, _} $point` is a compile error with message indicating `_` is meaningless in named destructuring (just omit the field)
E2e test file test/test_destructure_wildcard.c: tests using jacl_run() verify wildcard skipping, multiple wildcards, $_-reference error, named-destructuring-with-wildcard error
All existing tests pass
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra
userStories.notes: Builds on US-001. The parser already parses the pattern — it just needs to recognize bare `_` as a special token (not a variable name). The compiler change is small: when iterating pattern positions, if the name is `_`, skip emitting the extraction and local-add. For the skip mask: could encode as a bitmask operand to OP_DESTRUCTURE_VEC, or emit individual OP_VEC_GET only for non-wildcard positions (simpler).

userStories.title: Rest patterns in destructuring
userStories.description: As a JACL programmer, I want to use `..rest` to collect remaining elements during destructuring.
acceptanceCriteria: Parser recognizes `..name` (TOKEN_DOTDOT followed by identifier) in destructuring patterns
New opcode OP_DESTRUCTURE_VEC_REST with operand N: extracts first N elements individually, collects remaining into a new vector
`def [head ..rest] [vec 1 2 3 4]` binds head=1, rest=[vec 2 3 4]
`def [a b ..rest] [vec 1 2]` binds a=1, b=2, rest=[vec] (empty vector)
`..rest` must be the last element in positional pattern — compile error otherwise
Named rest: `def {x, ..rest} $point` binds x from field, rest is a map of remaining fields
`..` without a name (`def [head ..]`) is a compile error in positional patterns
Compile error if `..rest` appears more than once in a pattern
Rest collection creates a new vector (positional) or new map (named) — not a view/slice
`mut [head ..rest] $v` creates mutable bindings for both head and rest

E2e test file test/test_destructure_rest.c: tests using jacl_run() verify rest collection for vectors (basic, empty rest, many elements), named rest for structs/maps, error cases (not-last, unnamed, duplicate), mut rest
All existing tests pass
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra
userStories.notes: TOKEN_DOTDOT is already lexed. Parser change: when parsing a destructuring pattern and encountering TOKEN_DOTDOT, consume the following identifier as the rest-name. For positional rest: OP_DESTRUCTURE_VEC_REST N pops vector, pushes elements 0..N-1 individually, then pushes a new vector containing elements N..end. For named rest: after extracting explicitly named fields, collect remaining fields into a new map. The named-rest case for structs requires knowing all field names (from StructTypeRegistry) to determine which are 'remaining'.

userStories.title: Spread-all destructuring ({..})
userStories.description: As a JACL programmer, I want to use `def {..} $point` to import all fields of a struct into the current scope.
acceptanceCriteria: Parser recognizes `{..}` (TOKEN_LBRACE TOKEN_DOTDOT TOKEN_RBRACE) as a spread-all destructuring pattern
Parser also recognizes `{x, ..}` as explicit-plus-spread-all
Compiler resolves the struct type from the RHS expression and looks up all field names in StructTypeRegistry
Compile error if the RHS type is dyn/unknown — spread-all requires a known struct type
`def {..} $point` where Point has fields x,y creates bindings x and y in scope
`def {x, ..} $point` binds x explicitly, plus all other fields (y) — no duplicate binding for x
Shadowing rules apply: if x already exists in the same scope, `def {..} $point` is a compile error
E2e test file test/test_destructure_spread_all.c: tests using jacl_run() verify spread-all basic, explicit-plus-spread, shadowing error, dyn-type error, works with different struct types
All existing tests pass
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra
userStories.notes: Compiler-driven feature: the parser recognizes the pattern, but the compiler enumerates fields from StructTypeRegistry. For `{x, ..}`: compiler gets all fields from the struct type, removes `x` from the list, emits extraction for the rest. Same-scope shadowing check uses existing compiler__add_local error path. Once struct type is known, this desugars to extracting each field by name — reuses OP_STRUCT_GET_FIELD path from US-002.

userStories.title: Splat/spread in juxtaposition
userStories.description: As a JACL programmer, I want to spread a collection into separate arguments using `..` in `[]` juxtaposition mode.
acceptanceCriteria: Parser recognizes `..expr` inside `[]` command mode as a spread expression (new AST_SPREAD node wrapping the expression)
New opcode OP_SPREAD: pops collection (vector) from stack, pushes each element individually, pushes element count as i32 on top
New opcode OP_CALL_SPREAD: like OP_CALL but reads dynamic arg count from stack (sum of fixed args + spread counts)
Runtime stack overflow check before spreading: error if stack_top + spread_count >= STACK_MAX with message 'spread exceeds stack capacity'
`[+ ..$nums]` where nums=[vec 1 2 3] evaluates to [+ 1 2 3] = 6
Mix spread and regular args: `[+ 10 ..$nums 20]` = [+ 10 1 2 3 20] = 36
Multiple spreads: `[+ ..$a ..$b]` works correctly
Spreading empty vector produces zero arguments
Compile error if `..` has no following expression
Runtime error if spread target is not a vector (stream spread support added later in US-016)
E2e test file test/test_splat.c: tests using jacl_run() verify basic spread, mixed args, multiple spreads, empty spread, stack overflow error, non-iterable error
All existing tests pass
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra
userStories.notes: Parser change: in parser__parse_command() when inside [], if TOKEN_DOTDOT is encountered, parse the following expression and wrap in AST_SPREAD. Compiler: for each AST_SPREAD child in a command, compile the inner expression then emit OP_SPREAD. Track number of fixed args and number of spreads. After all args compiled, emit OP_CALL_SPREAD with the fixed-arg count; VM sums fixed + spread counts at runtime. The VM execution of OP_SPREAD: check jacl_is_vector, get length, check stack capacity, iterate and push each element, push count. OP_CALL_SPREAD: pop spread counts, sum with fixed count for total arity, proceed like OP_CALL.

userStories.title: Variadic proc parameters
userStories.description: As a JACL programmer, I want to define procs that accept variable numbers of arguments using `..rest` in the param list.
acceptanceCriteria: Parser recognizes `..name` (TOKEN_DOTDOT + identifier) as a rest parameter in proc param lists `{}`
Compile error if `..rest` is not the last parameter
Compile error if multiple `..rest` parameters in one param list
New opcode OP_COLLECT_VARIADIC with operand min_arity: at proc entry, collects args from index min_arity to arg_count into a new vector, binds as the rest parameter's local
Arity checking adjusted: minimum arity = number of non-variadic params (too few args is error, extra args collected)
`proc log {str level, ..msgs} { ... }` with `log "INFO" "a" "b"` binds level="INFO", msgs=[vec "a" "b"]
Zero variadic args: `log "INFO"` binds msgs=[vec] (empty vector)
Typed variadic: `proc f {..i64 nums}` type-checks each variadic arg at compile time when types known
Variadic procs compose with splat: `[log "INFO" ..$messages]` works correctly
E2e test file test/test_variadic.c: tests using jacl_run() verify basic variadic, zero extra args, typed variadic, splat-into-variadic, not-last error, multiple-rest error, too-few-args error
All existing tests pass
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra
userStories.notes: Parser: when parsing proc params in {}, if TOKEN_DOTDOT appears, consume the following identifier (with optional type prefix) as the rest param. Mark the proc's AST with is_variadic=true and rest_param_name. Compiler: emit OP_COLLECT_VARIADIC min_arity as first instruction in variadic proc body. This opcode reads actual arg count, creates vector from excess args, stores in rest param's local slot. The proc's registered arity should store min_arity + variadic flag so OP_CALL can skip the too-many-args check.

userStories.title: Stream value type and GC integration
userStories.description: As a JACL runtime developer, I need a stream value type that represents a lazy sequence, integrated with the GC and value system.
acceptanceCriteria: New JACL_TAG_STREAM (0x15) defined in value.c tag space
jacl_is_stream() predicate and jacl_stream_ptr() constructor defined
New OBJ_STREAM added to GCObjType enum in gc.c
JaclStream struct: state (STREAM_PENDING=0, STREAM_CONSUMED=1, STREAM_EXHAUSTED=2, STREAM_ERROR=3), next_fn (JaclVal closure), cached_value (JaclVal)
jacl_stream() constructor allocates via gc_alloc(heap, OBJ_STREAM, sizeof(JaclStream))
GC trace function for OBJ_STREAM pushes next_fn and cached_value onto mark stack
Exhausted/error streams have next_fn set to JACL_NIL to release producer state for GC
TYPE_STREAM added to JaclType enum in compiler.c
compiler__resolve_type() recognizes 'stream' keyword and [stream type] syntax (element type recorded, not enforced)
print on a stream outputs '<stream>' without materializing
Equality: streams use reference equality (identity comparison)
Second consumer pulling a CONSUMED stream gets runtime error: 'stream already consumed'
E2e test file test/test_stream_type.c: C API level tests verify stream creation, GC tracing (create stream + trigger GC + stream survives), print output, identity equality, consumed-state error
All existing tests pass
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra
userStories.notes: Model on JaclFuture: same pattern of GC object with state field and closure payload. Tag 0x15 is next available after JACL_TAG_ROPE_STRING (0x14). GC tracing: add case OBJ_STREAM in gc__trace_object in gc_collect.c — push next_fn and cached_value if non-nil. For print: add jacl_is_stream check in print dispatch. C-level tests can create a stream manually via jacl_stream(heap) and set next_fn to a test closure, without needing the full yield/CPS machinery.

userStories.title: OP_YIELD opcode and CPS-based stream creation
userStories.description: As a JACL runtime developer, I need OP_YIELD to create stream elements using the CPS transform, and suspension analysis must recognize yield as a suspension point.
acceptanceCriteria: New OP_YIELD opcode added to bytecode.c
compiler__suspension_analysis() recognizes 'yield' keyword as a suspension point (same as 'await')
Procs containing yield are marked as suspending and receive the implicit __k parameter
CPS transform in compiler__compile_cps_stmts() handles yield: creates continuation closure for code after yield, packages (yielded_value, continuation) into stream element
OP_YIELD in VM: pops value from stack, creates/updates JaclStream with value as current element and continuation as next_fn, returns control to consumer
New OP_STREAM_NEXT opcode: pulls next element from stream by calling stream's next_fn continuation, handles EXHAUSTED state
Calling a proc containing yield returns a JaclStream (generator entry: body doesn't execute until first pull)
Stream end: when producer returns normally, stream state set to EXHAUSTED
Yield from within for/while loops works correctly (continuation captures loop state via CPS)

E2e test file test/test_yield.c: tests using jacl_run() verify basic yield (proc yields 3 values then exhausts), yield in a loop, stream exhaustion, yield + collect produces correct vector, nested yield in conditionals
All existing CPS tests still pass
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra
userStories.notes: Most complex story. OP_YIELD mirrors OP_AWAIT: where await pops (continuation, future) and registers continuation as waiter, yield pops (continuation, value) and packages into stream. CPS transform creates continuation same way — compiler__compile_cps_stmts already splits remaining statements into continuation closure. Key difference: emit OP_YIELD instead of OP_AWAIT. VM handler: set stream->cached_value = yielded_value, stream->next_fn = continuation, return to caller. Generator entry: when a yield-containing proc is called, wrap body as stream whose first next_fn executes body up to first yield. Synchronous: producer and consumer same thread, OP_STREAM_NEXT calls continuation directly via runtime__setup_call + vm__run.

userStories.title: collect — stream to vector materialization
userStories.description: As a JACL programmer, I want to materialize a stream into a vector using collect.
acceptanceCriteria: 'collect' registered as a builtin command
collect on a stream: repeatedly calls OP_STREAM_NEXT until EXHAUSTED, accumulates into vector, returns vector
collect on a vector: returns the vector unchanged (no-op)
collect preserves element order
Type tracking: collect on TYPE_STREAM produces TYPE_VEC
Runtime error if collect called on non-vector non-stream value

E2e test file test/test_collect.c: tests using jacl_run() verify collect on yielded stream produces correct vector, collect on vector is identity, order preserved, empty stream returns empty vector, non-collection errors
All existing tests pass
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra
userStories.notes: Recommend native builtin proc for simplicity: register 'collect' with arity 1, implementation checks jacl_is_stream or jacl_is_vector, loops pulling from stream into RRB vector builder. Since collect calls OP_STREAM_NEXT which may call CPS continuations, the implementation needs to handle the synchronous call protocol.

userStories.title: Stream-aware for loop
userStories.description: As a JACL programmer, I want for to iterate over streams lazily, one element at a time.
acceptanceCriteria: VM dispatch for for-loop iteration checks value type: vector path unchanged, stream path added
Stream path: calls OP_STREAM_NEXT each iteration, executes body with element, loops until EXHAUSTED
O(1) memory: stream elements not buffered, only current element on stack
break inside for on a stream stops consumption (stream not fully exhausted)
continue skips to next OP_STREAM_NEXT pull
return from enclosing proc stops stream consumption
Implicit binding ($it) works: `for $stream { print $it }`
Explicit binding works: `for $stream item { print $item }`
HOF callback form works: `for $stream $callback`
Lambda form works: `for $stream [\ print $it]`
Compiler emits stream-specific path when TYPE_STREAM known at compile time

E2e test file test/test_stream_for.c: tests using jacl_run() verify for-over-stream basic, break mid-stream, continue, return-from-proc, implicit binding, explicit binding, lambda form, for-over-vector unchanged
All existing for-loop tests still pass
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra
userStories.notes: Current for-loop compilation (compiler.c lines 3888-4013) handles collection forms via iteration opcodes. Stream path replaces index-based iteration with pull-based loop: (1) OP_STREAM_NEXT, (2) check exhausted, (3) bind element, execute body, jump to (1). For break: LOOP_EXIT jump skips to after loop — stream remains partially consumed. Compiler can emit different bytecode for TYPE_STREAM vs TYPE_VEC, or runtime-dispatch opcode for TYPE_DYN.

userStories.title: Stream-aware filter
userStories.description: As a JACL programmer, I want filter to work lazily on streams, producing a new stream.
acceptanceCriteria: filter on a stream returns a new stream (not a vector)
Lazy: no elements consumed from source until result stream is iterated
Each pull on filtered stream pulls from source, tests predicate, skips non-matching, returns first match
filter on a vector returns a new vector (unchanged eager behavior)
Chained filters: `$s | filter $p1 | filter $p2` creates chain of lazy streams
Compose with pipes: `$stream | filter [\ > $it 2]`
Type tracking: filtering TYPE_STREAM produces TYPE_STREAM, filtering TYPE_VEC produces TYPE_VEC

E2e test file test/test_stream_filter.c: tests using jacl_run() verify lazy filter (only consumed elements pulled from source), chained filters, filter + collect correct vector, filter on vector unchanged, no-matches empty, pipe composition
All existing filter tests still pass
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra
userStories.notes: Stream filter creates new stream whose next_fn closure: (1) pulls from source via OP_STREAM_NEXT, (2) calls predicate, (3) if true yields, (4) if false loops. Closure captures source stream and predicate as upvalues. Recommend native proc creating JaclStream with C-level next function for simplicity. OP_FILTER dispatches on type: vector → eager, stream → create lazy filter stream.

userStories.title: Stream-aware transform
userStories.description: As a JACL programmer, I want transform to work lazily on streams, producing a new stream.
acceptanceCriteria: transform on a stream returns a new stream (not a vector)
Lazy: no elements consumed until result stream is iterated
Each pull on transformed stream pulls one element from source, applies fn, returns result
transform on a vector returns a new vector (unchanged eager behavior)
Compose with pipes: `$stream | transform [\ * $it 2]`
Chaining: `$s | filter $p | transform $f | collect` — fully lazy, single pass
Type tracking: transforming TYPE_STREAM produces TYPE_STREAM, TYPE_VEC produces TYPE_VEC

E2e test file test/test_stream_transform.c: tests using jacl_run() verify lazy transform, transform + collect correct vector, chained filter + transform pipeline, transform on vector unchanged, pipe composition
All existing transform tests still pass
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra
userStories.notes: Same pattern as US-012 but simpler: transform-stream next_fn pulls one element and applies function — no predicate loop. Shares implementation approach (native proc creating JaclStream). OP_TRANSFORM dispatches on type.

userStories.title: Sequence operations: count, take, first
userStories.description: As a JACL programmer, I want count, take, and first to work on both streams and vectors.
acceptanceCriteria: 'count' on stream: consumes entire stream, returns integer count
'count' on vector: returns vec-len (unchanged)
'take N' on stream: returns new lazy stream yielding at most N elements, doesn't pull until iterated
'take N' on vector: returns new vector with first N elements
'first' on stream: pulls one element, returns it (nil if empty)
'first' on vector: returns first element (unchanged)
All compose with pipes: `$stream | take 5 | collect`
Type tracking: take on stream → stream, take on vector → vector; count → i64; first → dyn

E2e test file test/test_stream_seq_ops.c: tests using jacl_run() verify count on stream and vector, take on stream (lazy — only N pulls), take on vector, first on stream and vector, take + collect pipeline, empty stream cases
All existing tests pass
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra
userStories.notes: count: loop OP_STREAM_NEXT until exhausted, incrementing counter. take: create stream with counter upvalue; each pull decrements, pulls source, yields; counter 0 → exhausted. first: single OP_STREAM_NEXT pull. All native builtins. take creates lazy wrapper stream, same pattern as filter/transform.

userStories.title: lines — string to line stream
userStories.description: As a JACL programmer, I want to split strings into line streams.
acceptanceCriteria: 'lines' registered as a builtin command
lines on a string: returns a stream that yields one line at a time (split on newline)
Handles both \n and \r\n line endings
Empty trailing line not emitted: 'a\nb\n' yields 'a', 'b' (not 'a', 'b', '')
Lazy: yields lines one at a time via index tracking, doesn't split entire string upfront
Compose with pipes: `"a\nb\nc" | lines | for [\ print $it]`

E2e test file test/test_lines.c: tests using jacl_run() verify lines basic, \r\n handling, no trailing empty, lines + for iteration, lines + collect, lines + filter pipeline, empty string yields empty stream
All existing tests pass
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra
userStories.notes: Create stream whose next_fn closure captures source string and current-index upvalue. Each call scans from current-index to next \n (or \r\n), yields substring, advances index. Index at end → exhausted. Skip final empty line by checking last char. Stream-to-stream lines (splitting incoming byte stream on newline boundaries) deferred to shell interop pass.

userStories.title: Compile-time stream/vector type enforcement
userStories.description: As a JACL programmer, I want the compiler to catch mistakes where I pass a stream to a vector-only operation.
acceptanceCriteria: Compiler checks argument type for vec-get, vec-set, vec-slice, vec-len, vec-push, vec-concat: if TYPE_STREAM, emit compile error
Error message: 'vec-get requires a vector; got stream (use collect to materialize)'
`collect $stream | vec-get 0` compiles successfully (collect changes type from stream to vec)
When type is TYPE_DYN, no compile error — runtime dispatch handles it (runtime error if stream passed to vec-only op)
Runtime error message for dyn-typed stream-to-vec-op matches compile-time message
Existing typed code still compiles correctly (no false positives)
OP_SPREAD updated to also accept streams: eagerly consumes stream into arguments (per resolved question 5B)

E2e test file test/test_stream_type_enforce.c: tests using jacl_run() verify compile error for typed stream to vec-get, successful compile for collect + vec-get, runtime error for dyn stream to vec-get, spread of stream works, all vec ops reject stream type
All existing tests pass
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra
userStories.notes: Compiler: in compilation of vec-get/vec-set/vec-slice/vec-len/vec-push/vec-concat builtins, after resolving collection arg type, check if TYPE_STREAM → emit error with helpful message. Runtime: in VM handlers, add jacl_is_stream() check before jacl_is_vector(), with descriptive error. For splat+stream: update OP_SPREAD in vm.c to handle jacl_is_stream() by pulling all elements via OP_STREAM_NEXT into temporary buffer, then pushing onto stack (with stack overflow check).
